components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; min-width:224px; min-height:68px; padding:0 22px; flex-direction:column; align-items:flex-start; justify-content:center; background:var(--amber,#ffb000); color:var(--canvas,#0d1214); text-decoration:none; transition:background 180ms ease-out,transform 180ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary span { font:700 .93rem var(--body,Inter,sans-serif); } .ds-btn-primary small { margin-top:3px; font:400 .68rem var(--body,Inter,sans-serif); text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:.08em; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background:#ffc33b; transform:translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--amber,#ffb000); outline-offset:4px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform:translateY(0); }

components.css: .ds-approach { position:relative; width:520px; max-width:100%; min-height:360px; overflow:hidden; color:var(--bone,#f4f0e5); background-color:#0a0f11; background-image:linear-gradient(rgba(244,240,229,.04) 1px,transparent 1px),linear-gradient(90deg,rgba(244,240,229,.04) 1px,transparent 1px); background-size:32px 32px; } .ds-approach svg { position:absolute; right:0; top:0; width:58%; height:100%; } .ds-road { fill:none; stroke:rgba(244,240,229,.18); stroke-width:22; } .ds-projection { fill:none; stroke:var(--amber,#ffb000); stroke-width:2; stroke-dasharray:5 9; animation:ds-route-dash 1.4s linear infinite; } .ds-range { fill:rgba(240,68,50,.07); stroke:rgba(240,68,50,.42); } .ds-camera { fill:var(--red,#f04432); } .ds-readout { position:absolute; z-index:2; left:24px; top:28px; width:220px; display:grid; grid-template-columns:auto 1fr; align-items:end; } .ds-readout strong { font:700 6.4rem/.8 var(--display,Oswald,'Arial Narrow',sans-serif); letter-spacing:-.04em; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; } .ds-readout>span { padding-left:8px; font:700 2rem/1 var(--display,Oswald,'Arial Narrow',sans-serif); } .ds-readout i { grid-column:1/-1; height:4px; margin:12px 0; background:var(--red,#f04432); } .ds-readout b { grid-column:1/-1; font:700 1.4rem/1.05 var(--display,Oswald,'Arial Narrow',sans-serif); } .ds-readout small { grid-column:1/-1; margin-top:9px; color:var(--red,#f04432); font:700 .56rem var(--body,Inter,sans-serif); letter-spacing:.07em; } @keyframes ds-route-dash { to { stroke-dashoffset:-28; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce) { .ds-projection { animation:none; } }

narrative.overview:
RoadCue is built as an engineered roadside instrument rather than a generic app-marketing surface. Matte charcoal fields, bone lettering, fine rules, vector paths, distance readouts, and signal geometry make direction and closing distance visible before the copy explains them. The atmosphere is calm and authoritative: technical enough to be credible, restrained enough to keep the warning legible.

The system is mostly flat and rectilinear. Contrast, scale, linework, and state color establish hierarchy; depth is reserved for device-shaped product surfaces nested inside the instrument field. The camera-location icon, route corridor, and signal arcs provide the recurring geometry. Police imagery, radar-gun motifs, generic map pins, gradient-led decoration, and fear-based visual drama are outside this world.
keyCharacteristics: Matte charcoal fields with bone text and hairline engineering rules.
Oswald compression for commands and readouts; Inter for explanation.
Signal red marks camera hazards; amber is reserved for active intent and focus.
Direction, distance, and alignment graphics turn product logic into interface.
Flat layouts yield to soft depth only for nested device surfaces.

rules.name: The Signal Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Red communicates camera hazard, amber communicates action or focus, and green communicates monitoring or completion; do not swap those meanings.

rules.name: The Bone, Not White Rule
rules.body: Use the warm bone neutral for principal light text and surfaces so the instrument remains calm rather than glaring.

rules.name: The Instrument Compression Rule
rules.body: Use Oswald wherever the interface must read like a command, sign, coordinate, or live measurement; use Inter for every sentence that explains what the product does.

rules.name: The Number-Is-Structure Rule
rules.body: Large tabular numerals are compositional anchors, not decorative statistics; preserve their alignment and terse unit labels.

rules.name: The Corridor Rule
rules.body: Give directional information a visible path through the composition: align major blocks to rules, tracks, or vertical movement instead of distributing them as unrelated cards.

rules.name: The Instrument Deck Rule
rules.body: Structural surfaces stay flat; shadow is reserved for nested device chassis, never for ordinary sections, rows, or calls to action.

rules.name: The Chassis Exception Rule
rules.body: Round only objects that read as a device, contained status control, signal node, or product icon; keep the surrounding information architecture rectilinear.

dos: Do keep the page grounded in matte charcoal, bone lettering, and engineered one-pixel rules.
Do reserve signal red for camera and hazard meaning, active amber for action and focus, and green for monitoring status.
Do make direction or distance tangible through route lines, vector movement, tabular readouts, and alignment.
Do preserve the Oswald/Inter division between compressed instrument language and explanatory prose.
Do keep the exact RoadCue camera-location icon as the identity anchor.
Do preserve the stacked 820px layout and compact 540px opening composition.
donts: Don't turn the system into a generic card grid, glassmorphic dashboard, or soft rounded app-marketing kit.
Don't use police imagery, radar guns, map-pin clutter, fear-based drama, or fabricated enforcement scenes.
Don't spread amber or green decoratively; their rarity makes their state meaning clear.
Don't add shadows to ordinary sections, rows, buttons, or navigation.
Don't replace the warm bone neutral with stark white or introduce unrelated accent colors.
Don't animate route movement without honoring `prefers-reduced-motion`.
